method: Full native-text keyword scan of body and footnotes; contextual reading of translator introduction, separable comments, temporary-marriage and Ahl al-Bayt passages
scope: Content screening; not an assertion that every sentence received full theological review

contextual_adjudications.finding: Temporary-marriage reports include explicit prohibition; mention of the subject is not doctrinal endorsement.
Ahl al-Bayt narration is supplied with a Muslim 2408 source citation; no added Shia doctrinal assertion identified in this passage.
The source glyph ص includes وآله in the blessing. A blessing on the family is not treated as sectarian evidence.

inside_hadith_screen.normalization: NFKC, removal of combining marks, Arabic/Persian kaf/ya and alef variants for retrieval only; quoted contexts retain exact consuming source strings

manual_contextual_adjudications.finding: Twelve caliphs, all Quraysh. The supplied narration and Persian translation do not name a line of twelve Imams, assert their infallibility, or add a Shia-specific identification.
Mantle and Quranic purification narration; no additional claim of Imam infallibility or divinely designated political succession is added.
Thaqalayn and care for the Prophet’s family, with the source’s clarification about wives and the families prohibited from receiving charity. No added sect-specific doctrinal claim identified.
Historical narration of Fatimah’s inheritance request, disagreement, Ali’s later reconciliation and pledge. Reporting the disagreement is not treated as a translator’s sectarian endorsement.
Ibn Masud and his mother were thought to belong to the household because of their frequent presence; no sect-specific doctrine.
Appointment retrieval matches are two competing caliphs and Allah’s care for Muslims during the Dajjal ordeal, not appointment of an Imam.
Occultation retrieval matches refer to a standing person, a worshipper standing in prayer, and backbiting (ghiba); none asserts an occulted Imam.
Other matched quantities concern angels, prayer units, months, Friday attendees, dowry, camels, group leaders and hypocrites; none supplies a doctrine of twelve Imams.
The candidate about insulting companions explicitly prohibits it: لا تسبوا أصحابي. This is not an endorsement of insulting companions.

The remaining Ahl al-Bayt keyword contexts concern ordinary households, charitable gifts, family responsibilities, permission for ruqya, sharing food and the narration vindicating Aishah. No added sect-specific doctrinal claim identified.
The explicit source-font blessing includes وآله. Family blessings and ordinary virtues are not classified as Shia-specific doctrine.

inside_hadith_screen.limitations: Targeted pattern retrieval followed by reading candidate passages and relevant surrounding source context; no claim that a comprehensive theological interpretation of every sentence was independently certified.
